# The Poseidôn file: from poseidon to the temple it became
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *poseidon*. This is the file on how **Poseidôn** replaced it.

Poseidôn's myths dramatize the rage of the excluded. He is a great Olympian, yet he is repeatedly thwarted — by Athena at Athens, by Odysseus after the blinding of Polyphemus, by the very mortals whose sacrifices he demands. After the defeat of the Titans, Zeús, Poseidôn, and Hádês divided the cosmos by lot.  Zeús took the sky, Hádês the underworld, and Poseidôn the sea.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Poseidôn
- **ASCII form:** poseidon
- **Meaning:** "Lord of the Earth (from πόσις + δᾶ)"
- **Domain of influence:** Sea, Earthquakes, Horses
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Ποσειδῶν
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 197 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ποσειδῶν**. On the evidence, it means "Lord of the Earth (from πόσις + δᾶ)".

Strip **Poseidôn** to *poseidon* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ô** — Circumflex: long omega with stress: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Poseidôn** lives at [/sites/poseidon/](/sites/poseidon/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/poseidon/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/poseidon/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/poseidon/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Poseidôn** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** — Lord of the waters that surround and threaten every Greek city; the sea itself, with a temper and a trident.
- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — Ennosigaios, the Earth-Shaker; earthquake and tsunami risk was his remit before it was an industry.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — Rising seas are his encroachment; the coast's oldest adversary in a warming century.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
